title: Reverse each full block of k, then move group_prev to the block's new last node
caption: k = 3 on dummy → a … g. Blocks [a b c] and [d e f] are reversed; the short tail [g] stays as it is.

frames.text: group_prev starts at the dummy, the node before block 1. Look 3 nodes ahead: a, b, c exist, so the block is full.
Block 1 reversed (prev started at d, so c b a already points on to d). dummy.next = c, the new front; group_prev = a, the block's new last node.
Block 2 [d e f] is full too: reversed to f e d, a.next = f, and group_prev moves to d.
Only g is left after group_prev: fewer than k nodes, so stop and leave it unchanged. The answer is dummy.next = c.
